items.title: Kerala High Court upholds relief to Wipro over 'Brahmins' sambar powder trademark
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld the temporary injunction imposed on Greenmount Spices, restricting it from using the ‘Brahmins’ or ‘Brahmins Sambar Powder’ trademarks until a trademark infringement suit filed by Wipro Enterprises is decided. [ Greenmount Spices Private Limited v. Wipro Enterprises Private Limited ] Justice CS Dias opined that Wipro had established a prima facie case to support its claim of prior commercial use of the trademarks in question. " I am satisfied that the respondent has established a prima facie case, supported by materials indicating prior commercial use of the ‘Brahmins’ trade mark. The balance of convenience is also in favour of the respondent. If the impugned use is ultimately found to infringe the respondent’s [Wipro] rights, its continued use may erode the distinctiveness of the trade mark and cause injury not readily compensable in damages. These conclusions are tentative and shall not prejudice the final adjudication of the suit, " the Court said in its judgment. items.title: Kerala cops arrest BLM co-op society chairman in Chennai for alleged fund diversion
items.summary: The Kerala Crime Branch Police on Thursday, October 29, arrested R Premkumar, founder chairman of Bharath Lajhna Multi State Cooperative Society, one of the leading co-operative societies in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Premkumar was taken into custody from his residence in Chennai. Crime Branch officials, however, refused to divulge details of the case. The case is being probed by the Economic Offences Wing of Crime Branch, Kozhikode. A team led by DySP, Crime Branch, EOW, arrested Premkumar. Following the arrest, Premkumar complained of physical discomfort and was shifted to a hospital. As per reports, funds worth Rs 300 crore were siphoned off to the private accounts of Premkumar. The money collected as deposits from members of the cooperative society was diverted for purchase of resorts and theatres, allegations said. The case began with the former CEO Naveen S Nair filing a complaint with the Nadakavu police station in Kozhikode against Premkumar and a few others for physically attacking him. items.title: MP Owaisi seeks transparent plan to tackle El Niño impact on Hyderabad’s water supply
items.summary: Hyderabad MP and All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi has called for a clear plan to address drinking water security in Hyderabad and surrounding urban areas, as well as a dedicated summer action plan that includes urban employment guarantee provisions to deal with the impact of El Niño on Telangana. In an October 28 letter to Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka, who is heading the Cabinet sub-committee charged with dealing with the drought and El Niño conditions across Telangana, Owaisi made several suggestions, including a dedicated urban summer action plan addressing the specific vulnerabilities of Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Malkajgiri and the surrounding urban regions. Amid concerns over drinking water security for Hyderabad and the Core Urban Region, Owaisi called on the government to publish a dedicated drinking water plan for the summer season for Hyderabad and surrounding urban areas, including source-wise availability, zone-wise supply schedules, and cut-off dates for contingency sourcing, through a public-facing dashboard. items.title: Kochi private buses race, road users at risk
items.summary: Kochi has a frequent and active network of private city buses. However, commuters in the city also have to contend with the aggressive and reckless driving style of Kochi's private buses. Drivers hurry to reach their destinations at high speed, often without considering other vehicles on the road. Minor accidents and near-miss incidents have become very common on these roads. Commuters in Kochi city complain about unnecessary honking, sudden overtaking, and minor accidents involving private buses, especially during peak hours. According to a statement issued by the Kochi police, they registered 2,003 cases against bus crew members during inspections conducted between September 9 and 30. Among these, 130 cases were registered for competitive driving, and 71 involved dangerous or negligent driving. Speaking to TNM, KM Siraj, Private Bus Owners Association, Ernakulam District secretary, said there is no system on our roads to maintain a safe distance between buses, two-wheelers, and cars. "Such systems may exist on national highways, but there is no such arrangement in cities," he added.
